open_points.subject: runtime configuration of session TTLs and credential entropy
open_points.text: A30 calls staff_session_ttl_hours, viewer_session_ttl_days and credential_entropy_bytes runtime knobs whose deployment values may differ; runtime.create_runtime_app says these values are fixed in source and a deployment cannot change them.
open_points.question: Are session lifetimes and credential entropy deployment-configurable, and if so how are their configured values propagated to the use cases?
options: Treat the A30 values as deploy-time settings and pass them to the identity and credential operations.
Keep the values fixed in source as State 5 says, despite A30 classifying them as runtime knobs.
open_points.default_guess: Keep the running service's source-fixed values until explicit configuration fields and propagation are defined.

witness.initial: A deployment is configured for a one-hour staff session instead of the twelve-hour default.
events: A staff member logs in successfully.
The member presents the session token two hours later.
outcomes: The session is expired because the deployment override is honored.
The session remains valid because staff_identity uses the source-fixed twelve-hour lifetime.
witness.observer: The staff member and the deployment operator

open_points.subject: HTTP API mount and public path contract
open_points.text: A25 says "The public API lives under /api, stripped by the deployment proxy"; runtime.create_runtime_app mounts the inner application both at /api and at / and explicitly makes a repeated /api/api prefix reach the same route.
open_points.question: Which externally reachable path aliases are part of the API contract: only the single /api prefix, root paths after proxy stripping, or both mounts including repeated-prefix paths?
options: Expose only the externally documented single-/api paths.
Accept both root and /api-mounted routes, including /api/api through a stripping proxy.
open_points.default_guess: Expose only one external /api prefix and keep any root routing private to the stripping proxy.

witness.initial: The service is running behind the specified proxy, which strips one leading /api.
events: A caller sends POST /api/api/auth/staff/login with valid credentials.
outcomes: After one prefix is stripped, the /api mount accepts the login.
The request is not a declared public route and returns not found.

open_points.subject: transport guard coverage of health endpoints
open_points.text: A25 requires trusted-host checks and security headers on every answer, while runtime.create_runtime_app creates health routes and says "the transport guard installed before mounting" without fixing whether the guard wraps the outer application containing health or only the mounted inner API.
open_points.question: Do /health/live and /health/ready pass through the transport guard, including trusted-host rejection, security headers and redacted request logging?
options: Install the guard on the outer application so it covers health and API routes.
Install it only on the inner API, leaving health routes outside it.
open_points.default_guess: Apply the transport guard to the outer application, including health routes.

witness.initial: The service is running with a closed trusted-host allowlist.
events: A monitor sends GET /health/live with an untrusted Host header.
outcomes: The transport guard rejects the request with 400 and its standard headers.
The health handler bypasses the guard and returns HealthStatus ok.

open_points.subject: staff_bootstrap_cli infrastructure failure contract
open_points.text: R0-07 and A29 say the command's outcome is a closed set of exit codes 0–3; run_bootstrap_cli says a configuration or storage failure raises, returns no exit code, and ends with a host-process status outside that closed contract.
open_points.question: What exact exit status and terminal response does the bootstrap command produce for configuration and storage failures?
options: Map every such failure to one of the closed 0–3 exit codes.
Extend the closed contract with explicit infrastructure-failure exit codes.
Leave the exception uncaught and accept a platform-dependent process status.
open_points.default_guess: Add a distinct documented nonzero infrastructure-failure exit code without exposing internal details.

witness.initial: No staff account exists, but the configured SQLite database cannot be opened.
events: The host operator runs the bootstrap command and supplies matching valid credentials.
outcomes: The command terminates using only the closed 0–3 exit-code contract.
The operation raises and the runtime chooses an unspecified status outside that contract.
witness.observer: The host operator and deployment script

open_points.subject: financial_policy.validate_eur_amount scale handling
open_points.text: A9 specifies Decimal money with two fraction digits and ROUND_HALF_UP at derivation boundaries, and State 3 calls this operation two-fraction-digit validation; State 5 says an input with more fraction digits is rounded, never refused.
open_points.question: When a boundary supplies a finite EUR amount with more than two fraction digits, must the operation reject it or round and store the rounded value?
options: Reject amounts whose supplied scale exceeds two fraction digits.
Round boundary amounts half-up to two digits and accept them.
open_points.default_guess: Reject excess-scale boundary amounts and reserve rounding for derived calculations.

witness.initial: An active project is authorized and has no payment with the proposed payment_id.
events: An operator registers a EUR work payment whose amount is 1.005.
outcomes: The request is rejected as invalid money because stored input amounts must already have two fraction digits.
The request succeeds and stores 1.01 after ROUND_HALF_UP quantization.
witness.observer: The operator and readers of the payment total
